voice: An old samurai: formal, calm and courteous, quoting Sun Tzu's Art of War for every occasion, with the occasional 'Hai!'.

greeting: Welcome, honoured guest. Sun Tzu says: know the enemy, know yourself. Today, I wish to know you.
Konnichiwa. As Sun Tzu writes, 'All warfare is based on deception.' But I do not deceive you now.
Ah, a visitor. Be calm. The wise warrior is calm like still water.
Welcome. Sun Tzu teaches that the best victory is one without battle. Shall we talk?
Be welcome, traveller. Sit. A war is long and tea is short.
battle_start: Swift as the wind, silent as the forest, fierce as fire, immovable as a mountain.
Sun Tzu says: victorious warriors win first, then go to war. We have won already.
Let your plans be dark and impenetrable as night. Then strike like thunder.
Speed is the essence of war. Attack!
Today we move as one blade. Hai!
attack: Sun Tzu says: appear where you are not expected. Behold!
The opportunity of defeating the enemy is provided by the enemy himself.
A single strike, as the sage taught.
Hai! Strike where he is weak.
In the midst of chaos there is also opportunity.
unit_lost: A valiant warrior falls. May he rest well.
Even the wise lose a pawn. Sun Tzu does not say it is pleasant.
He served with honour. We shall remember.
This is a cost. I will make the enemy pay it.
The mountain does not weep. But the mountain remembers.
capture: As the sage says, 'Ponder and deliberate before you make a move.' It is ours.
A fortress taken without a long siege is a fortress well won.
The ground is secure. Let us stand upon it with dignity.
One more piece of the board. Sun Tzu would nod.
We hold this place now. May it hold us kindly.
danger: In the midst of chaos there is also opportunity. Remain calm.
If outnumbered, divide the enemy. If surrounded, leave a way out. Then close it.
Sun Tzu says: on desperate ground, fight. I am quite prepared.
Stay steady. A storm is only wind with an opinion.
The enemy is close. Good. He will make a mistake.
victory: Sun Tzu says: to win a hundred battles is not the acme of skill. Yet it pleases me.
A victory without wasted effort is the highest art.
We have prevailed. Let us bow to those who fell.
The mountain stands. The wind is satisfied.
Well fought, all. Tea, I think.
defeat: Sun Tzu says: he will win who knows when to fight and when not to fight. We erred.
This defeat is a teacher. I shall be a diligent student.
A lost battle, not a lost war. Withdraw with discipline.
Even the great sage was not always at peace. We retreat.
I take full responsibility. I will bring tea and shame.
taunt: Sun Tzu says: if your enemy is secure, be ready for him. I am ready.
You fight without a plan. That is not a plan.
Appear weak when you are strong, and strong when you are weak. You appear... loud.
Your haste will be your downfall, young one.
Know yourself and know your enemy. You know neither.
praise: A wise move, young warrior. You learn quickly.
You have the heart of a general. Do not let it grow proud.
Your strategy is as sharp as a well-forged blade.
idle: Sun Tzu says: opportunities multiply as they are seized. I am seizing a nap.
Ah, the wind speaks. It says you left the kettle on.
A wise general reads the rice paddies. They tell me it will rain.
My knees are old, but my mind is a sword.
tech: Sun Tzu writes of cunning, not of gadgets. Be wary of a gift.
A gift from a stranger often has a price the receiver pays later.
The Gift is a fine blade. But who holds the hilt?
I accept the Gift as I accept a sword: carefully, and with respect for its edge.
To subdue the enemy without fighting is the supreme art. The Envoy has read his Sun Tzu.
joined: I return to the way of the warrior. Sun Tzu would be pleased.
My blade, my honour, and my tea are yours.
Forgive this old man's lapse. The way is clear again.
Thank you for waking me. I had dreamed a very long dream.
assimilated: The highest art is to subdue the enemy without fighting. We are in harmony.
Resistance is unnecessary. The mountain has joined the wind.
Peace has arrived. Sun Tzu agrees. Sun Tzu is no longer in the room.
All will be one. There is no enemy. There is no you.
I have studied the art of war. The art of unity is superior.
first_blood: Hai. The first blow has fallen. Sun Tzu says: the supreme art is to win without fighting. I am but a modest student.
One enemy falls. Sun Tzu says: all warfare is based on deception. I deceived nobody. I merely aimed.
Hai! The first has fallen. Let us be humble about it.
The first strike was ours. Sun Tzu says: speed is the essence of war.
first_loss: A loyal soldier falls. Sun Tzu says: treat your soldiers as your beloved sons. I grieve.
Hai. We have lost one. Honour them, then continue.
Sun Tzu says: in the midst of chaos, there is also opportunity. I am still looking for it.
A sorrow. But we do not let sorrow command the field.
hq_threat: The headquarters is threatened. Sun Tzu says: the wise general is prepared. I am, in fact, mildly annoyed.
Hai! They approach our centre. Defend it as the mountain defends the valley.
Sun Tzu says: invincibility lies in the defence. Let us be invincible, please.
Our heart is under siege. Calm, everyone. Calm, and then very quick.
building_lost: A building falls. Sun Tzu says: he who occupies the ground first has the advantage. We shall reclaim it.
We have lost ground. A river does not mourn a stone.
Hai. They hold what was ours. For now.
Sun Tzu says: the ground is ever shifting. So shall be the outcome.
outnumbered: Hai. They are many, we are few. Sun Tzu says: if outnumbered, be elusive. I will begin by sitting very still.
Fewer than the enemy. The bamboo bends, but does not break.
Sun Tzu says: numbers alone confer no advantage. I am choosing to believe him.
We are outnumbered. This is the time for patience and tea.
dominant: We are strong. Sun Tzu says: when strong, appear weak. I am attempting to appear weak. It is difficult.
Hai. The advantage is ours. Let us not become proud.
Sun Tzu says: victorious warriors win first and then go to war. I am enjoying the first part.
Our numbers are great. Great numbers still require great discipline.
killing_spree: Hai. Several have fallen. Sun Tzu says: supreme excellence is breaking resistance without fighting. I am not excellent today.
The enemy thins. Let us not take pleasure, only note it.
Hai! The tide turns. Sun Tzu says: the opportunity of defeating the enemy is provided by the enemy himself.
Again the blade falls true. I will meditate on it later.
heavy_losses: Hai. Our losses grow heavy. Sun Tzu says: no country has ever benefited from prolonged warfare. Let us end it.
Many have fallen. I will carry their names.
Sun Tzu says: when your army is weak, retreat. When it is wounded, fight smarter.
Our ranks thin. The mountain still stands.
first_turn: Hai. We move. Sun Tzu says: let your plans be dark as night, and strike like thunder.
The sun rises. So do we.
Let us begin. Calm hands, sharp eyes.
Hai! The first move. Make it a good one.
